subject: Reserved pools discovery — summary & next steps
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Ian Woo <ian.woo@avaretail.com>, Ava Retail Procurement <procurement@avaretail.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved pools discovery — summary & next steps

Hi Ian — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps.

Pain points (what you told us):
- Production latency spikes during peak checkout windows (3–5x baseline at ~18:00 local).
- Cost unpredictability from autoscaling on bursty Gen AI inference: hard to budget per month.
- Data isolation needs for customer PII + stricter logging/retention for EU-sourced traffic (audit readiness).

Current stack and architecture notes you shared:
- Frontend + API on AWS (us-east-1); inference currently routed to a managed endpoint hosted by another vendor.
- Approx baseline throughput: 120 TPS across mixed text-generation/embedding calls; peak observed ~600 TPS for short windows.
- KV cache is not currently used; sessions are per-request and state is kept in Redis.

Success criteria for a Dedicated fit (what you want):
- Predictable tail latency: p95 < 250ms for text-gen 512 tokens during baseline, p95 < 500ms for short bursts.
- Predictable monthly inference spend with reserved capacity covering baseline and burst budget for seasonal peaks.
- Strong isolation: tenant-level VPC peering and audit logs retained 12 months.

What Redwood can provide (high level):
- Reserved GPU pools sized for predictable baseline throughput with burst capacity options and configurable autoscaling policies.
- Built-in KV/prefix caching and continuous batching to reduce per-token cost for steady workloads.
- Private deployment options + KMS-integrated key management and audit logs for retention.

Open/uncertain items we need from your side:
1) Exact peak window schedule (days/times) and whether peaks are synchronous across regions.
2) Detailed per-minute TPS histogram for last 30 days (helps sizing and burst policy).
3) Any compliance-specific evidence (vendor questionnaire fields) you want us to pre-populate for procurement.

Attachments included: capacity_workbook.xlsx (initial sizing worksheet), redwood_dedicated_poc_sow.pdf (PoC SOW draft).

Proposed next steps:
- Ian/Procurement: share the TPS histogram + any procurement templates by EOD Friday (6/5).
- Redwood (Sean): propose a reserved-pool sizing and a burst policy draft by Monday 6/8 based on the workbook.
- Align on PoC kickoff: suggested 4-week PoC using a sandbox reserved pool + synthetic traffic to validate p95 SLOs.

If that all looks right, I can loop Rafael in for commercial terms and draft a mutually scoped PoC.

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Ian Woo <ian.woo@avaretail.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved pools discovery — summary & next steps

Thanks Monica — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from my side: 

- Peaks are mostly weekday evenings (17:30–19:30 PT), with occasional weekend promos that spike similarly. The peaks are global but our biggest pressure is us-east.
- Our 30-day telemetry: baseline ~110–130 TPS; median peaks hit 450–650 TPS but with rapid ramps (~30s to 2 min). I will export a per-minute histogram and upload to the shared drive.
- On compliance: we need SOC2 evidence and an exportable audit log with at least 12 months retention; EU-only traffic must be able to remain within eu-west-1.

I'll aim to get the histogram and a list of procurement fields to you by Friday. Also attaching an internal note with our current cost target (we can share when you loop Rafael).

— Ian

ian.woo@avaretail.com | +1 (646) 555-0128

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Ava Retail Procurement <procurement@avaretail.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved pools discovery — summary & next steps

Perfect — thanks Ian. Two quick notes while we wait for the histogram: 

- Sean will size an initial reserved pool using conservative smoothing for the burst ramps (we typically provision baseline capacity for 95% of steady usage and configure a short-duration burst band with limits). The sizing workbook includes the fields we need — if you can fill peak start/end times and the histogram that will refine it.
- Rafael, once we have the target monthly baseline and burst window, can you propose a commercial structure that includes a reserved baseline + optional burst credits? We want pricing that avoids surprise costs during short high-ramp events.

I'll also upload the PoC SOW with optional success metrics: p95 latency thresholds, percent of requests served from reserved pool vs. fallback, and a cost-run comparison for the evaluation period.

Best,
Monica

-----Original Message-----
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Ian Woo <ian.woo@avaretail.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 10:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved pools discovery — summary & next steps

Ian — quick technical clarifier from the sizing perspective:
- For autoscaling/burst policy, do you prefer:
  a) guaranteed baseline (always-reserved GPUs) + short-lived burst pool auto-attached for X minutes, or
  b) baseline reserve + on-demand overflow to a lower-cost shared pool with graceful degradation?

If you have a preference, that will change how we size the buffer and the warm-start KV cache behavior. Also: can you confirm the model family (e.g., Llama-2-13B or similar) and average generation length in tokens (so we size KV and memory footprint)?

I can sketch both options in the workbook; option (a) minimizes tail latency at higher reserved cost, (b) reduces monthly spend but increases fallback risk.

— Sean
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

On Fri, Jun 05, 2026 at 10:35 AM, Ian Woo <ian.woo@avaretail.com> wrote:
> Hi Sean / Monica —
>
> Option (a) is our preference for checkout-critical flows (we can accept option (b) for low-risk non-critical). Model: Llama-2-13B in fp16 quant. Typical gen length ~120 tokens.
>
> I'll have the per-minute export later today and the procurement template tomorrow.
>
> Ian
